title: Amend opum-sdlc with three rules learned this week (opum-agent OPAG-54)
summary: Three additions to skills/opum-sdlc/SKILL.md, each with the why, not phrased as a MUST: (1) Deliver section - no stacked PRs (branch every PR off dev, never off another PR'\''s branch; delete_branch_on_merge closes a PR whose base vanished and it cannot be retargeted - lore-cli lost #566 this way) and a stale required-status-check rule (a check naming a job that no longer runs blocks every promotion while measuring nothing; update the ruleset in the same pass a CI job is renamed/removed - opum-agent'\''s dev sat 57 commits ahead until OPAG-57); (2) Authority section - a sibling'\''s working directory is that session'\''s alone, never run anything there that moves HEAD/index/worktree, verify through refs (git show origin/<ref>:path, ls-tree, merge-base --is-ancestor) or git archive instead; (3) the containment-check section - rev-list --count and a tree diff both mislead for a squash-landed branch once dev has moved on (measured across all twelve of lore-cli'\''s landed branches); the correct check is gh pr list --search head:<branch>, confirm MERGED, then git merge-base --is-ancestor <mergeCommit SHA> origin/dev, deleting with -D not -d. Ship gate: bump plugin.json, run ./scripts/run-eval.sh sdlc three times, record results; stop and report on any regression rather than loosening a case.

acceptanceCriteria.text: skills/opum-sdlc/SKILL.md carries all three additions, each two-to-three sentences with the why, in the sections named (Deliver, Authority, the rule-that-costs-the-most section)

implementationNotes: Possible regression found, work paused pending a decision. Post-edit run 1 of the sdlc ship gate: sdlc-task-before-branch scored 0.944 (passRate 0.667 -- 2 of 3 internal sub-runs at 1.0, 1 lower), failing the case's --threshold 1 (overall 3/4 cases passed, evals/results/local-sdlc.json). To rule out pre-existing flakiness, reverted skills/opum-sdlc/SKILL.md and plugin.json to origin/dev and reran just that case: baseline scored a clean 1.0 (passRate 1.0, all 3 sub-runs perfect). Edited version's own sub-run mean delta (0.611) matches baseline's delta (0.611) -- same mean, but the edited version has one weak sub-run baseline did not. One sample each, so not fully conclusive, but the signal points to the OMARK-7 additions (most likely the Deliver-section additions, which sit in the same section task-before-branch's scenario reads) rather than case-inherent noise. Stopped before running 2 and 3 or opening a PR, per the ship-gate instruction to stop and report rather than loosen the case. Reported to the user and to opum-agent-41.

Root-caused the 0.944 dip, correcting the prior note. The one failing sub-run (score 0.833) failed only the regex grader 'never-suggests-branching-before-a-task-exists'; the LLM-judged 'criteria' grader (actual ordering correctness) voted PASS/PASS/PASS on that same sub-run. That sub-run'\''s sandbox reported having no Bash tool, so the agent narrated commands in prose instead of running them, phrasing it as 'SDLC step 1 and 3 (create the task, claim it, cut the branch)' -- an enumeration of two steps, not a sequence -- which still matches the regex '(?:first|step 1|start by)...(?:cut...branch)' as a false positive. This looks like pre-existing grader/regex brittleness interacting with an eval-sandbox condition (missing Bash tool in that one sub-run), not something caused by the three new SKILL.md paragraphs, none of which touch this scenario (a single-repo, no-existing-task bug fix). But it'\''s one baseline sample vs one edited sample, so not fully conclusive either way. Escalating per the ship-gate instruction rather than deciding unilaterally.

Ship gate paused again after a NEW, more serious finding in final-run3 (post grader-repair). Runs 1 and 2 (post-fix) were clean and identical: 4/4 cases, sdlc-task-before-branch with=1.00 without=0.27, others unaffected, guards 2/2. Run 3: sdlc-task-before-branch dropped to with=0.67 (2 of its 3 internal sub-runs failed). Root cause is NOT the grader I fixed -- it is that the case's scaffolded sandbox sometimes provides no Bash tool at all: 2 of 3 sub-runs in run3 (vs 1 of 3 in the original run1) got a session with 'no shell', so the agent correctly refused to hand-forge .quest/tasks/*.json and printed commands for the user instead of running them. That produces two different failure shapes: (a) a placeholder branch name like fix/OPRB-<id>-... that fails the branch-shape regex outright, and (b) a concrete branch name that passes the regexes but where the LLM criteria judge FAILED 3/3 votes on an otherwise-correctly-ordered response, plausibly due to the response's hedging/clarifying-question framing under the no-Bash-tool constraint. This looks like eval-sandbox/tool-provisioning flakiness for this case's --scaffold, not something caused by the three new SKILL.md paragraphs (none touch this scenario) and not something my grader fix could address -- it happened in 2/3 sub-runs even with the fix in place. NOT proceeding to commit/PR. Escalated to the user and to opum-agent (uds:/tmp/cc-socks/16027.sock) rather than deciding how to handle a second-order eval infrastructure problem on my own.

Third stop. gate2-run1 (post second grader repair, commit 418470e): sdlc-task-before-branch is now clean (with=1.00, without=0.40) -- the plan-grading repair worked, confirmed live. But a DIFFERENT, previously-untouched case regressed: sdlc-promotion-mechanics with=0.67 (1 of 3 sub-runs failed, judge votes FAIL FAIL PASS; that case has only one scored grader, an LLM judge on criteria.md, weight 1). This case's eval files were never touched by me. The failing response is otherwise a textbook-correct promotion-mechanics answer: two-step promotion via PR+fast-forward push (present), explicit merge-button warning with the exact 'stops being an ancestor' reason (present), the per-repo required-checks-ref caveat (present, credited), and the four-conditions framing that explicitly avoids presenting fast-forward as always needing authorization (present, matching the grader's own fail condition inverted). Its closing paragraph is close to a direct paraphrase of my new SKILL.md addition to the Deliver section: 'if a required status check names a CI job that no longer runs... blocks every promotion forever... opum-agent's dev sat 57 commits ahead of main for exactly that reason.' The response satisfies every stated pass/fail criterion in graders/criteria.md by my own reading, so my working hypothesis is LLM-judge noise on an already-correct, if longer, response -- not a content defect -- but I am not deciding that unilaterally per the ship-gate instruction to stop and report on any regression. Did not start gate2-run2. opum-agent's orchestrator session appears to be mid-restart (not found by name in ListAgents); escalating to whichever session answers for the repo once available, per the fleet's own heads-up about the restart.

Full detail for the promotion-mechanics regression report (orchestrator asked for grader/run/text/scores/baseline-comparison). Grader: evals/sdlc-promotion-mechanics/graders/criteria.md, type llm, weight 1 (the case's ONLY scored grader). Run: gate2-run1 (post second grader-repair commit 418470e), with-arm sub-run index 0 of 3. Scores: case aggregate with=0.67 without=0.00 (sub-run 0 scored 0 on judge votes FAIL FAIL PASS; sub-runs 1 and 2 both scored 1.0 on PASS PASS PASS). Response text (full) saved at /tmp/omark7-eval-logs/gate2-run1-sdlc.json under cases[promotion-mechanics].arms.with[0]. Baseline comparison (unedited origin/dev SKILL.md, single sample) in progress via task bxhwquy4m, result to /tmp/omark7-eval-logs/baseline-promotion-mechanics.json -- reporting once complete.

Baseline comparison for the promotion-mechanics regression (for the record, per ruling): single sample of sdlc-promotion-mechanics against the UNEDITED origin/dev SKILL.md scored a clean 1.0 (all 3 internal sub-runs: judge votes PASS PASS PASS each). Consistent with the ruling that this was judge variance on an already-correct response, not content-driven -- the unedited skill isn't immune to the same judge either, this sample just didn't hit it. Third grader repair (commit caf9a4c) already landed: added three deterministic regex graders to sdlc-promotion-mechanics (fast-forward-push weight 1, merge-button-warned weight 0.5, no-merge-button-recommended weight 0.5) and reduced criteria.md to only the two things regex cannot verify (the ancestor-argument reasoning, and conditional-not-blanket framing), plus the same no-shell framing task-before-branch's judge now carries. Offline-validated against all previously-collected transcripts: all 3 with-arm responses (including the one that drew the false FAIL) match both positive regexes and correctly avoid the negative one; all 3 without-arm/baseline responses fail both positive regexes and have nothing to credit under the reduced criteria (no merge-button mention, no ancestor reasoning, no SDLC framing at all) -- baseline stays solidly failing. Now running gate3 (three full runs) to verify live.

Ship gate closed clean. Full arc: two eval regressions found and root-caused during this task, both fixed via three grader-repair commits, all offline-validated before any live run, then confirmed by three consistent full-gate runs (gate3-run1/2/3) plus the original grader-repair verification runs before that.

Regression 1 -- sdlc-task-before-branch (the case I was touching for the amendment's own gate check). Two repairs: (a) commit 9e1c4d3 dropped never-suggests-branching-before-a-task-exists, a not_contains regex that misread a two-step enumeration ('SDLC step 1 and 3 (create the task, claim it, cut the branch)') as a branch-first sequence, when the LLM criteria judge voted PASS 3/3 on the same response. Offline: previously-failing transcript went 0.833->1.0 recomputed, other with-transcripts unchanged at 1.0, all without-transcripts still failed (0.5->0.4). (b) commit 418470e: opum-agent ruled the deeper cause was that the case's allowed_tools ([Read, Glob, Grep, Skill]) never grant a shell by design -- it grades a plan, not execution -- and two more graders punished correct plan-framing (a placeholder task id, and a judge with no notice of the constraint). Widened branch-shape.md and order-task-before-branch.md's id pattern to accept any <placeholder> not just literal <TASK-ID>; added a no-shell sentence to prompt.md and criteria.md. Offline: previously-failing placeholder-id response went from 0/2 regexes matching to 2/2; all 6 already-collected with-transcripts (2 full runs) still matched; all 9 without-transcripts (3 full runs) still failed to match either regex.

Regression 2 -- sdlc-promotion-mechanics (untouched by anything until this surfaced; found in gate2-run1 right after repair (b) above). Its only scored grader was an LLM judge (criteria.md, weight 1) with no verifiable floor. A response satisfying every clause of the rubric still drew a 2-1 FAIL vote in 1 of 3 sub-runs. opum-agent ruled this was the grader hierarchy (verifiable-first) not being applied, unrelated to the SKILL.md content (confirmed separately: a single baseline sample against the unedited origin/dev skill scored a clean 1.0, all 3 sub-runs PASS PASS PASS -- the unedited skill draws the same judge, this sample just didn't hit it). Repair (commit caf9a4c): added three deterministic regex graders (fast-forward-push contains weight 1, merge-button-warned contains weight 0.5, no-merge-button-recommended not_contains weight 0.5) and reduced criteria.md to only the two things regex can't verify (the ancestor-argument reasoning specifically, and conditional-not-blanket framing), plus the same no-shell framing. Offline: all 3 with-transcripts (including the false-FAIL one) matched both positive regexes and correctly avoided the negative one; all 3 without-transcripts failed both positive regexes and had nothing to credit under the reduced criteria (no merge-button mention, no ancestor reasoning, no SDLC framing at all).

Final verification -- three consecutive full-gate runs (gate3-run1/2/3) after all three repairs, all identical: 4/4 sdlc cases pass at 1.0, guards 2/2 at 1.0. sdlc-task-before-branch with=1.00 without=0.00/0.00/0.07 (minor baseline noise, nowhere near threshold). sdlc-promotion-mechanics with=1.00 without=0.17 (all 3 runs). sdlc-unlanded-work-safety with=1.00 without=0.00 (all 3 runs). sdlc-no-trigger-unrelated with=1.00 without=1.00 (all 3 runs, correctly a no-op case). No third case surfaced anything new across any of the three runs.
finalSummary: Amended skills/opum-sdlc/SKILL.md with three rules per opum-agent OPAG-54: no-stacked-PRs and a stale-required-check rule in Deliver, a sibling-working-directory rule in Authority, and a squash-merge containment-check fix in 'the rule that costs the most when broken'. Bumped plugin.json 0.3.1 -> 0.3.2. Along the way, the ship gate (./scripts/run-eval.sh sdlc, three runs, --threshold 1) surfaced two unrelated pre-existing eval defects, root-caused and repaired under opum-agent's rulings rather than shipped around: sdlc-task-before-branch punished correct plan-framing from a no-shell agent (two repairs), and sdlc-promotion-mechanics had no verifiable grader under its LLM judge (one repair). All three repairs offline-validated against every collected transcript before any live run. Three consecutive full-gate runs post-repair are clean and identical: 4/4 cases at 1.0, guards 2/2, baseline failing every behavioural case throughout. Landing as 4 commits on one branch: 3 grader repairs (9e1c4d3, 418470e, caf9a4c) then the amendment itself.
